$$

Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2\times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PB{P}^{-1}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Block Diagonalization of a 3x3 Matrix
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/7014ce766be779f4231c78a99a6e013bfc48bfd9e21da7fa565c49e466437c99.png)
Consider the matrix $A$ shown above. Find a block diagonal matrix $B,$ where the $2 \times 2$ block represents a rotation-scaling matrix, such that $A=PBP^{-1}.$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\color{red}\lambda_1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${\color{red}{\mathbf{v}_1}},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\color{blue}\lambda_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\lambda}_{\color{blue}3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${\color{blue}\mathbf{v}_2} = \overline{\color{blue}\mathbf{v}}_{\color{blue}3},$ then $A=PBP^{-1},$ where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071697/assets/5e03c481312af462a0739b4670e24325d2e06cc10449c65bfb04208206fc5d58.png)
Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

To compute the eigenvalues of $A,$ we solve the characteristic equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda  & 5 \\ -1 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )^{2}-1(-1)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the real eigenvalue is 
$\lambda_1={\color{red}-1}.$
Now, using the quadratic formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{2,3} & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{(4)^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 5}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2} \\  & =\frac{-4\pm 2\text{i}}{2} \\  & =-2\pm \text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the block diagonal matrix is

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=5\pm 7\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4\pm 6\text{i} \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
